render_assessment: Rolled view (yaw -30, pitch 10, roll +35): at rest the Milky Way band runs upper-left to lower-right, i.e. the horizontal band of the forward view turned clockwise on screen, which is what a +35 camera roll (camera CCW about its view axis) must do; the stars and the band turn together, no seam. At 0.99c the headlight sits upper-left at about (230, 195) px; my oracle puts the velocity direction (0,0,-1) at (255.8, 196.0) px for that view, and the brightest concentration is there; the band converges on it and is blue-shifted. Off-axis view (yaw 50, pitch 25): at rest the band sits low across the frame; at 0.99c the whole sky has drained toward the bottom-right edge, where my oracle places the headlight at (987, 450) px, just off the right edge at the right height. Forward references unchanged from M1.4d. No artefacts, mirrored stars or NaN blobs at any speed on the contact sheet (5 views x 4 speeds).

independent_verification.method: float64 Python oracle (scratch oracle.py) written from spec section 2 and Godot's documented YXZ Euler order R = Ry(yaw) Rx(pitch) Rz(roll), right-handed; pinhole with vertical fov 70, 960x540 (f = 385.69 px). Compared against the PR camera driven by a scratch Godot probe (FreeLookCamera.project, is_behind, hud_line, view_velocity_angle, and Godot's own Camera3D.unproject_position). Not derived from the PR's code.
independent_verification.velocity: (1,1,-1)/sqrt3 at 0.99c, 4 arbitrary galaxy-frame star directions, 5 orientations
independent_verification.agreement: oracle vs PR CPU projection within 2e-4 px on all 16 visible cases (float32 Vector3 inputs account for the residual); Godot's float32 unproject within 3e-4 px
independent_verification.spec_check_values_through_rolled_camera: 90-degree source on the camera's right, camera along v, roll 0/+30/-115: 25.8419 deg off centre at 0.9c and 60.0000 at 0.5c, dy = 0 px (stays on the screen horizontal) in the oracle; the PR test asserts the same to 2e-3 deg
independent_verification.roll_sign: Oracle: a star 20 deg right of the unrolled view with roll +30 lands at dx = +121.544, dy = +70.174 px (below centre, y down), i.e. positive roll turns the camera CCW and the sky CW on screen. The PR's CPU gives the same numbers, Godot's own basis (unproject_position, which is what VIEW_MATRIX on the GPU inverts) agrees to 3e-4 px, the HUD prints roll +35.0 for the capture view whose render shows the band turned clockwise, and the golden's rolled orientations pass at 0.102 px. CPU, GPU and HUD share one sign convention.
independent_verification.cpu_reference_independence: FreeLookCamera's CPU path is explicit float64 Euler trigonometry (R^T applied as Rz^T Rx^T Ry^T) plus a pinhole f = H/2 / tan(fov/2); the GPU path is Godot's VIEW_MATRIX (inverse of the node's float32 Basis.from_euler) times PROJECTION_MATRIX with the quad offset in the shader. They share only the three angles and fov, not code; the aberration on both sides mirrors spec section 2 by design (CLAUDE.md gate 3). One caveat: in _golden_offaxis the star is placed by deaberrating the aim, so the CPU 'expected' is the grid point by construction; the CPU projection of a non-trivial aberrated direction is exercised by test_physics (against Godot's unproject) and by my oracle, not by the golden itself.

non_blocking.issue: project() does not guard the behind-camera case; depth <= 0 yields a mirrored or infinite pixel with no signal. The golden and tests only pass directions in front, so this is latent.
non_blocking.suggestion: assert/early-return on c[2] >= 0 (or document that callers must check is_behind() first)

non_blocking.issue: the public API takes and returns float32 Vector3 (view_dir, screen_right/up, project's n, view_velocity_angle's heading); the docstring says 'float64 scalars' which is true only inside _rotate/_to_camera. Fine at 0.75 px / 0.1 deg, but precision rule 5 readers will expect the caveat.
non_blocking.suggestion: one line in the docstring: inputs/outputs are float32 Vector3, rotation and projection are float64; residual ~1e-7 rad

non_blocking.issue: expected = project(aberrate(deaberrate(aim))) is the grid point by construction, so the golden checks the GPU aberration against the CPU inverse but never a non-trivial CPU projection of an aberrated direction.
non_blocking.suggestion: add 2-3 fixed galaxy-frame directions per orientation whose expected pixel comes from project(aberrate(n)) with n not derived from the grid (my oracle values above can seed them)
